questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes You must answer on the multiple choice answer sheet. You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS  There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
What is an example of market failure?

options.A: a firm incurring a loss by selling goods at prices below the average cost
options.B: a guaranteed price that results in the accumulation of unsold stocks
options.C: low income earners being unable to buy high-priced goods
options.D: under-provision of a socially desirable good

questions.questionText: What is likely to prevent the development of an effective cartel in an industry?

options.A: a high concentration ratio
options.B: a limit-pricing policy
options.C: high fixed costs
options.D: low barriers to entry

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm’s cost and revenue curves. The firm changes its objective from profit maximising to revenue maximisation. MC price Z AR = P = D X Y O MR quantity Which area on the diagram will show the increase in total revenue?

options.A: X + Y + Z B Y C Y + Z D Z

questions.questionText: Which statement about the downward sloping demand curve of an inferior good is correct?

options.A: Negative income effect and substitution effect move in opposite directions, leading to a steeper demand curve.
options.B: Negative income effect and substitution effect move in the same direction, leading to a flatter demand curve.
options.C: Positive income effect and substitution effect move in opposite directions, leading to a steeper demand curve.
options.D: Positive income effect and substitution effect move in the same direction, leading to a flatter demand curve.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the private and social costs and benefits of production in a free market that result in market failure. MSC costs, benefits MPC MSB MPB O K L M N output Which change in output would be necessary to overcome this market failure?

options.A: from K to M
options.B: from M to N
options.C: from M to L
options.D: from N to L

questions.questionText: Aprofit-maximisingmonopolymakesanabnormalprofitanddecidestoreinvestsomeofthisprofit to improve its capital stock. What are the most likely outcomes from this change? allocative dynamic productive efficiency efficiency efficiency

options.A: improves improves improves
options.B: unchanged improves improves
options.C: improves unchanged unchanged
options.D: unchanged unchanged improves

questions.questionText: What is not an example of government failure?

options.A: decreased maximum price causing producers to leave the market
options.B: higher guaranteed price encouraging suppliers to overproduce
options.C: increased minimum wage leading to employers dismissing workers
options.D: increased subsidies encouraging the consumption of a socially desirable product

questions.questionText: When does a more equal distribution of income occur?

options.A: when a country’s income tax system is made more progressive
options.B: when someone is made better off without making someone else worse off
options.C: when the best use is made of scarce resources
options.D: when there is an increase in the Gini coefficient

questions.questionText: What is not a reason for imposing a tax on producers based on the amount of pollution caused in the production process?

options.A: Firms have a financial incentive to reduce pollution.
options.B: It is relatively hard to administer and monitor this tax scheme.
options.C: Some firms cause less pollution than others.
options.D: Taxes on pollution reduce negative production externalities.

questions.questionText: A government introduced a tax on soft drinks containing sugar. It was forecast that the tax would raise £520m per year for the government. However, the tax received was £240m. What is the most likely reason why the tax collected was lower than forecast?

options.A: a specific tax instead of an ad valorem tax was introduced
options.B: fewer drinks than originally forecast contained sugar
options.C: most retailers did not increase the price of soft drinks
options.D: the demand for soft drinks was price inelastic

questions.questionText: A government’s aim is to reduce real wage rates. Which policy should be used to achieve this aim?

options.A: Award public sector workers pay increases below the rate of inflation.
options.B: Encourage private sector pay awards to be in line with company profits.
options.C: Introduce a minimum hourly wage for non-unionised, low-paid workers.
options.D: Remove any restrictions on trade unions to bargain for wages.

questions.questionText: How is marginal revenue product calculated?

options.A: marginal physical product × marginal revenue
options.B: marginal physical product ÷ price
options.C: total physical product × marginal cost
options.D: total physical product ÷ marginal cost

questions.questionText: A teacher currently earns $30000. She would be willing to continue in that teaching job, provided she earned at least $25000. Also, she would prefer to remain a teacher than change to her next best alternative employment as an accountant where she could earn $40000. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Her economic rent as a teacher is $5000.
options.B: Her economic rent as an accountant is $10000.
options.C: Her transfer earnings as a teacher are $30000.
options.D: Her transfer earnings as an accountant are $15000.

questions.questionText: What does the accelerator principle explain?

options.A: how changes in consumption lead to changes in income
options.B: how changes in income lead to changes in consumption
options.C: how changes in income lead to changes in investment
options.D: how changes in investment lead to changes in income

questions.questionText: The diagram shows an economy’s production possibility curve. output of capital Y goods X O output of consumer goods What causes a movement from point X to point Y?

options.A: a positive output gap
options.B: a recession
options.C: actual economic growth
options.D: potential economic growth

questions.questionText: Inthequantitytheoryofmoneyequation,MV=PT,Visdefinedastheincomevelocityofcirculation. Which change would tend to reduce the value of V?

options.A: a move to monthly rather than weekly salary payments by firms
options.B: an increase in interest rates
options.C: an increase in the use of cash machines to reduce money balances held
options.D: a decrease in the use of credit cards by individuals

questions.questionText: What is likely to improve the occupational mobility of labour?

options.A: a decrease in income tax that increases aggregate demand
options.B: a decrease in unemployment benefit
options.C: an increase in retraining schemes for the unemployed
options.D: more advertising of employment vacancies in the economy

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a closed economy with no government. It is in initial equilibrium when the national income is $1000 million. 45° planned C + I expenditure C = 100 + 0.8Y $million I = 100 0 500 1000 national income $million If the full employment national income occurs at $800 million, what is the value of the inflationary gap?

options.A: $40 million B $160 million C $260 million D $840 million

questions.questionText: If prices increase in country X but stay the same in country Y, what will be the most likely impact on the internal and external value of money in country X? internal value external value of money of money

options.A: falls falls
options.B: falls rises
options.C: rises falls
options.D: rises rises

questions.questionText: Which policy may increase economic growth without causing inflation?

options.A: giving subsidies to producers
options.B: increasing government spending
options.C: lowering direct taxes
options.D: lowering interest rates

questions.questionText: The current account on the balance of payments moves into deficit. What is a possible reason for this?

options.A: a decrease in tax revenue
options.B: export-led growth
options.C: repayment of debts to other countries
options.D: the import of new technology

questions.questionText: Which policy would not lead to an increase in the value of a country’s currency?

options.A: an increase in domestic inflation
options.B: an increase in domestic interest rates
options.C: an increase in incomes abroad
options.D: an increase in tourists visiting the country

questions.questionText: In an economy with unemployed resources the marginal propensity to consume is 0.2. The government increases its budget deficit and finances it by selling bonds to the non-bank private sector. What is the likely consequence of this?

options.A: The currency will depreciate, increasing exports and reducing the trade deficit.
options.B: The increase in real output will be limited as the value of the multiplier is low.
options.C: The money supply will fall, leading to a reduction in aggregate demand.
options.D: There will be a decrease in the rate of interest, causing demand-pull inflation.

questions.questionText: Which components are included in the current account and financial account of the balance of payments? current account financial account

options.A: official reserve assets and trade in services and transactions trade in goods in official reserve assets
options.B: primary income and official reserve assets and trade in goods secondary income
options.C: trade in goods and foreign direct investment and trade in services secondary income
options.D: trade in services and portfolio investment and secondary income official reserve assets

questions.questionText: The graph plots the Gini coefficient and GDP per head for three countries, X, Y and Z. What can be concluded from the graph? 0.75 Y Gini coefficient X 0.50 Z 0.25 GDP per head

options.A: Average incomes are higher in country X than in country Z.
options.B: Country X is the least developed country.
options.C: Income is equally distributed in country Y.
options.D: The distribution of income in country Y is more even than in country X.

questions.questionText: What is least likely to lead to an increase in optimum population?

options.A: an improvement in labour productivity
options.B: an improvement in the quality of capital and technology
options.C: an increase in birth rate and a fall in death rate
options.D: an increase in the availability of natural resources

questions.questionText: What is not included as a weighted indicator of poverty in the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)?

options.A: cooking fuel
options.B: electricity
options.C: medication
options.D: water

questions.questionText: Which role is performed by the World Bank but not by the International Monetary Fund (IMF)?

options.A: facilitating free trade among member countries
options.B: providing assistance to member countries to plan fiscal policies
options.C: providing bailout packages to countries facing external account challenges
options.D: providing monetary assistance to member countries to build infrastructure

questions.questionText: Some economists argue there is little evidence of the value of aid in improving economic development in less-developed countries. Which situation supports this claim?

options.A: Capacity to benefit from transfer of communications technology has increased.
options.B: Investment in infrastructure has created transport links and port facilities.
options.C: Over-reliance on technical assistance has impaired local initiatives and innovation.
